h1: The 8 Best 240V Portable Power Stations for Home Backup and Big Loads, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 large portable power stations scored on 240V output, capacity, expandability, recharge speed and home backup features.
summary: The PECRON E3800LFP is the best 240V portable power station here, with 3,840Wh, 4,200W and a clear 120/240V listing. The BLUETTI Apex 300 is the modular alternative with switchable voltage, the PECRON Two E3600LFP bundle brings a 240V hub and two batteries, and the OUPES Guardian 6000 V2 is the choice for transfer-switch home backup.
intro: The costliest mistake in this category is buying on watt-hours and finding out afterwards that the unit only produces 120V. A well, a dryer, an RV air conditioner or a 240V welder will not run from a 120V outlet, however large the battery is. Voltage is a feature, and some listings state it clearly while others leave you to find out from the manual.

Eight large power stations went through the spec sheets here, scored on confirmed 240V output, capacity, expansion, recharge speed and backup features. Where a listing does not say 240V output outright, we say so and ask you to confirm before buying. None of this is a substitute for an electrician when you connect to a home panel.

products.name: PECRON E3800LFP Portable Power Station, 3840Wh, 120/240V 4200W
products.description:
The E3800LFP holds 3840Wh and delivers 4200W with a listed 120/240V output. It is expandable to 53.76kWh, has 14 ports and is controlled with an LCD touchscreen or an app. A full charge takes about 1.4 hours at 3200W AC.

It ranks first because it is the only unit here that pairs explicit 120/240V with the biggest continuous output short of the OUPES and a fast recharge. LFP chemistry, indicated by the model name, is the long-life battery type favoured for home backup, since it tolerates far more charge cycles than older lithium types. The cost is weight and price: this is a rolling appliance, not a camping cooler.

Buy it if you want 240V for a well pump, a dryer or a workshop. Skip it if you only need to power laptops and lights.

products.name: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station, 2764.8Wh 3840W
products.verdict: Switchable 120V/240V in one system, with an ecosystem of batteries and chargers.
products.description:
The Apex 300 stores 2764.8Wh and outputs 3840W, with 120V/240V switchable in a single system. It expands through the B300K and B500K batteries, and the ecosystem includes a Hub D1, Charger 1 and 2, and SolarX 4K.

It ranks second because the modularity is the point: you can start with one unit and grow into a home backup system, with solar input when you are ready. The capacity is smaller than the PECRON, and the accessories add up in cost, so the starting price is not the whole bill. The upside is clarity about voltage and a supported expansion path.

Buy it if you plan to build up a system over time. Skip it if you want the most capacity in a single box.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want to grow a system over time.
products.skipIf: You want the most watt-hours in one box.

products.name: PECRON Two E3600LFP Power Stations with 240V Double Voltage Hub
products.verdict: Two 3,072Wh units and a 240V hub for 6,144Wh combined, with a 1.3 hour recharge.
products.description:
This bundle pairs two E3600LFP power stations of 3072Wh each with a 240V double voltage hub. The units charge fully in about 1.3 hours at 3200W AC and expand to 15,360Wh.

It ranks third because the 240V comes from combining two 120V units through the hub, which adds equipment and a cable layout to learn. The reward is 6144Wh in the box and a recharge time most single units cannot match. Compared with the E3800LFP, you manage two machines and two batteries, but you can also use them separately for different jobs.

Buy it if you want to run 240V now and keep the flexibility of two separate units. Skip it if a single-box setup is simpler for you.
cons: Two units to store and move
products.skipIf: You prefer one box and one cable.

products.name: OUPES Guardian 6000 V2 Portable Power Station, 4608Wh, 6000W
products.verdict: 6,000W and 4,608Wh with direct transfer switch integration for whole-home backup.
products.description:
The Guardian 6000 V2 offers 4608Wh and 6000W, expandable to 41,472Wh, with a 64 minute full recharge claim. The listing highlights direct transfer switch integration, which is the route to powering a home panel.

It ranks fourth because the highest output in the ranking is wasted if you cannot confirm the voltage. The listing does not spell out 240V output in the part we reviewed, so confirm that on the product page before buying. The transfer switch feature and the 6000W rating make it the strongest candidate for whole-home backup once that is verified.

Buy it if you plan a professionally installed transfer switch. Skip it if you need explicit 240V confirmation before you commit.
products.idealFor: Whole-home backup with a transfer switch.

products.name: Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus Portable Power Station, 3600W, 3584Wh
products.verdict: Ceramic membrane cells tested to 302 degrees F, in a wheeled luggage-style body.
products.description:
The HomePower 3600 Plus holds 3584Wh, outputs 3600W and expands to 21kWh. Its distinctive points are ceramic membrane cells tested to 302 degrees F and a wheeled luggage-style design.

It ranks fifth because the safety claim is the most specific in this group, and the wheels make a heavy unit practical to move. The listing we reviewed does not confirm 240V output, so check before buying if that is the reason you are shopping. Compared with the PECRON, it has similar capacity but a less clear voltage story.

Buy it if safety and mobility matter and you have confirmed the voltage you need. Skip it if 240V is non-negotiable and unverified.
pros: Wheels ease moving a heavy unit

products.name: AFERIY 3840Wh Portable Power Station, Expandable to 11520Wh
products.verdict: 3,840Wh and 3,600W, UL Listed, with a 1.5 hour full recharge and 7-year support.
products.description:
The AFERIY 3840Wh delivers 3600W, expands to 11.5kWh and recharges fully in 1.5 hours at its fastest. It is UL Listed and comes with 7-year support.

It ranks sixth because a UL listing is the sort of certification you want on a unit that runs inside your home. The expansion limit is lower than the PECRON, and, like the Jackery, the listing does not confirm 240V in the part we reviewed. It does beat many rivals on its support period.

Buy it if a recognised safety listing and long support matter to you. Skip it if you need to expand far beyond 11.5kWh.
products.skipIf: You need a very large expandable bank.

products.name: AFERIY P280 Portable Power Station, 2800W (Peak 5600W)
products.verdict: 2,048Wh with a NEMA TT-30 outlet and a 38 minute 0 to 80 percent charge.
products.description:
The P280 provides 2048Wh and 2800W with a 5600W peak, expandable to 10.24kWh. It carries a NEMA TT-30 industrial outlet and charges 0 to 80 percent in 38 minutes.

It ranks seventh because the TT-30 is an RV-style 30 amp 120V outlet, so it does not by itself indicate 240V output. The fast charge is the highlight, and the expansion headroom is generous. The base capacity is the smallest in the top bracket after the P210.

Buy it if you have an RV or similar load that uses a TT-30 plug. Skip it if you must have true 240V.
products.idealFor: RV owners with a TT-30 plug.
products.skipIf: True 240V is the reason you are shopping.

products.name: AFERIY P210 Solar Generator, 2048Wh Portable Power Station, 2400W
products.verdict: A 48.5 lb, 2,048Wh unit with 16dB idle noise and a 7-year extended warranty.
products.description:
The P210 stores 2048Wh and outputs 2400W with a 4800W surge, at 48.5 lbs. It runs at 16dB under normal load and 30dB at full load, with a 7-year extended warranty.

It ranks last because the listing does not confirm 240V output, and the capacity is the smallest here. What it does well is portability and quiet: at 48.5 lbs it can still be lifted by one person, and 16dB is close to silent. It is the unit to take on a camping trip, not to wire into a house.

Buy it if you want a quiet, relatively portable station for big devices. Skip it if you need 240V or whole-home backup.
products.idealFor: Quiet portable power for camping and vans.

methodology.title: Voltage output
methodology.description: We looked for listings that state 120/240V output outright, and treated unconfirmed voltage as a risk, since it decides whether a well pump or dryer will run.

methodology.title: Capacity and expansion
methodology.description: Base watt-hours and the stated expansion ceiling were compared for backup runtime.

methodology.title: Recharge speed
methodology.description: Full-charge times at AC input were weighed, because a fast refill matters during an outage.

methodology.title: Safety and support
methodology.description: UL listings, cell safety claims and warranty terms were read as evidence of build quality.

methodology.title: Home integration
methodology.description: Transfer switch compatibility, hubs and app control were scored for whole-home use.

whatMatters.detail: A 240V appliance needs a split-phase or true 240V source, and most portable stations only offer 120V. Look for the words 120/240V or a 240V hub in the listing, as on the PECRON and BLUETTI units. If the listing is silent, ask the maker before buying.

Continuous output is what the unit can sustain, while surge is a brief peak for motor starts. A 2,800W unit with a 5,600W peak can start a well pump, but not run a large oven. Add up your appliances' running watts and aim for headroom.

Watt-hours set how long you can run, and expansion lets you add batteries later. A 3,840Wh unit runs a 400W load for roughly nine hours in theory. Check the stated expansion limit for your growth plans.

LFP cells tolerate thousands of cycles and run cooler than older lithium types. The PECRON models are named for it. For a unit that sits in a garage as backup, longevity matters more than the last bit of weight savings.
Connecting a power station to a home panel needs a transfer switch and a qualified electrician. The OUPES lists direct transfer switch integration. Never back-feed a panel through a dryer outlet.

cards.text: Confirmed 120/240V output, LFP cells, a transfer switch option and enough expansion to carry a fridge, a furnace blower and a well pump overnight.

cards.text: The PECRON E3800LFP is the clearest all-round pick, with the OUPES Guardian 6000 V2 as the high-output option once its voltage is confirmed.

faq.q: Can I run a well pump on a portable power station?
faq.a: Many well pumps are 240V and need a high surge to start. A unit with confirmed 120/240V, such as the PECRON E3800LFP, is the safer choice. Check the pump's startup watts against the surge rating.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one for 240V?
faq.a: Buying on capacity alone. Many large stations are 120V only, and a 240V appliance will not run on them. Look for an explicit 120/240V statement or a 240V hub.

faq.q: Is the BLUETTI Apex 300 worth it over the PECRON?
faq.a: If you want to grow a system over time with a supported ecosystem, yes. The PECRON offers more base capacity in a single box. Pick on how you plan to expand.

faq.q: How do I connect one to my house?
faq.a: Use a transfer switch installed by a licensed electrician. Never plug a power station into a wall outlet to back-feed the house. The OUPES lists transfer switch integration for this reason.

faq.q: How should I store a large power station?
faq.a: Keep it in a cool, dry place at a partial charge and top it up every few months. Avoid freezing and direct heat. LFP units tolerate storage better than older lithium chemistries.
Most accept solar input, and the BLUETTI lists SolarX 4K in its ecosystem. Check the maximum solar input wattage and voltage window on each listing before you buy panels.

finalTake: For a home that needs real 240V, the PECRON E3800LFP is the portable power station to buy, with 3,840Wh, 4,200W and a clear 120/240V listing. The BLUETTI Apex 300 is the right choice for a system you want to grow, and the PECRON Two E3600LFP bundle suits those who like flexibility. The OUPES Guardian 6000 V2 is the high-output option for transfer-switch backup once you confirm voltage. Verify the 240V output on the product page before you pay.
